score.description: Final plan score per the rubric: 10.0 minus the sum of deductions, one decimal place

verdict.description: pass if `findings` has NO critical or high, otherwise fail. Previous findings still open must be repeated in `findings`, so they count. The score does NOT affect the verdict: a plan with score 6.5 and only medium/low findings is a pass

summary.description: 2-4 sentences in English: the main thing the critic thinks about the plan

deductions.description: Breakdown of the score. Empty array only when score = 10.0

weight.description: Positive number: how many points were deducted for this item, the weight from the rubric

reason.description: What exactly was deducted for, in English, concretely

previous_findings.description: Rounds 2-3 only (empty array in round 1): the status of EVERY finding from your previous round. A finding that is still open or whose rejection you dispute MUST also be repeated in `findings` under the same id and severity: the verdict, the score and the blocking count are computed from `findings` only

id.description: The id from the previous round, e.g. C3

status.description: closed: the plan now handles it, or it was rejected with a fact you accept; open: not handled; rejection_disputed: rejected, but the justification is factually wrong

note.description: One line in English: the fact behind the status (plan section, path:line)

findings.description: Findings on the plan. Each must be an action, not an observation

id.description: Short identifier like C1, C2, C3, so a finding can be referenced in the reply

severity.description: Defect class strictly per the rubric. critical and high BLOCK the plan and require BOTH a concrete failure_scenario AND either trigger=normal_use or harm of a dangerous class. Dangerous classes (block at any likelihood, never downgraded): access to another user's or customer's data or actions; bypass of authentication, a signature check or permissions, including fail-open; a secret leak; money, balance, payments (races, double charges, missing idempotency); irreversible loss or corruption of data; a deploy or a write to an external system without the user's yes. critical = breaks production or loses data / hole in isolation or permissions; high = a critical project rule is violated, plan logic defect, unverified assumption about an external system on which access control or the data source depends; medium = load without an estimate, coverage gap, other unverified assumptions, AND any finding whose scenario is a rare_coincidence with recoverable harm outside the dangerous classes, AND findings about the review procedure itself (smoke-test method, plan wording, approval marks); low = incomplete description and cosmetics. A critical/high without a failure scenario is downgraded to medium

trigger.description: When the failure scenario happens: normal_use = an ordinary action, a retry, a deploy, an expected cron overlap, a second user; rare_coincidence = needs a rare coincidence (same person in two tabs in the same second, a crash at one exact line, a narrow race window); n/a = medium/low findings without a failure scenario

title.description: One line in English: the gist of the finding

detail.description: Why this is a problem and what will happen if left as is. A concrete failure scenario, not generalities

failure_scenario.description: Under which inputs or state what exactly breaks: concrete, in English. Required for critical and high: without it the finding counts as an observation and is downgraded to medium. For medium and low the string '—' is acceptable

evidence.description: The finding's anchor in the REPOSITORY as path:line (for example src/billing/cache.ts:87): what exactly in the code confirms the defect. If the finding concerns the plan text and there is no anchor in code, write 'plan only' and explain in detail why code is not enough. A critical/high finding without a code anchor or without an explanation of why there is none is weakened and must be downgraded

plan_section.description: Which step or section of the plan it refers to. '—' if the whole plan

suggested_fix.description: What exactly to change in the plan. This is an edit to the PLAN, not to code
